page.layout: One printed page. Running head at the top, centred right. Below it, one column of text with a short verse, a signature, a rule, and a poem with its heading. Catchword at the right foot.

p.i: Magni versibus aureis Horatî, Sic possis mihi semper inuidere.
AD Cœnam curte quoties inuito recufas, Ad te si currens vsque vocatus eo? Forte cibi viles, tenuis vel certè sodalis Forte Corrugant nares rustica tecta tibi:
Quódque auro nobis nullo laquearia fulgent, Stromata, nec vestis conchiliata nitet.
Non hac, crede, vetat te ad nos accedere causa: Verum vis quod tu nos faciamus idem.

main_text.head: DE FELICE PERNETO, olim caprario, nunc Pontifice Romano, Xisto seu Sixto V.

p.i: CAPRA Ioue uberibus nutriit, pro munere tāto Capram sideribus Iupiter inserit. Pontificem Sixtum vaga & inconsulta creauit Capra peroratis ordine suffragiis. Capram Roma colat, Caprinum quæ sibi legit Pontificem, male olens hircus vt imperitet. Arcanum quæris! Sathanas sic debuit ipse Romanum cunctis nobilitare gregem.

page.notes: The word "certè" in the third line of the first poem is struck through in the print. The second number "69" at the top is uncertain and may not belong to this page's sequence. The mark over the "i" in "Horatî" is uncertain. "hac" in "Non hac" may be a ligature or an æ; I read it as printed. "nutriit" has a j-like form in the print and may read "nutriit". The "De" at the right foot is a catchword, cut off by the scan edge. The verse lines are italic throughout, and the poem title is in roman capitals.
